reasons: A narrowly better supports long phone writing: its normal phone view uses the full content area for source, whereas B divides it into two roughly 360-pixel-high panes that each truncate the long sample text.
A labels the phone transition explicitly as Read preview and Back to editor. B offers Reading and retains both panes in normal mode; this exposes the relationship but fragments long-document work.

Both variants show all named actions and clear Markdown/HTML download choices, readable document hierarchy, balanced desktop columns and constrained desktop reading widths. No preference was awarded merely for colors, decoration or panel style.

coverage.method: Viewed each supplied PNG individually at its original dimensions with view_image.

limitations: Screenshots do not establish functional correctness for rendering, import/export, persistence, sharing, shortcuts or spell check.
Touch hitboxes, focus behavior, scroll behavior and software keyboard effects were not exercised.
Longer documents than the visible sample were not observed.
API/DOM/vendor compatibility and fidelity to the original brand cannot be verified from the supplied images.
The preference is narrow and rests principally on observed phone workspace allocation.
